You are helping reproduce the open-source project **python-paillier** (package name `phe`, version 1.5.0,
by CSIRO's Data61) in the directory /workspace. It is a Partially Homomorphic Encryption library
implementing the Paillier cryptosystem, licensed GPLv3.

A reference copy of the *installed* library source is readable at
/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/phe/ (files: __about__.py, __init__.py, util.py, encoding.py,
paillier.py, command_line.py). READ IT to get the API exactly right. Do NOT modify anything under
/usr/local/lib. Do NOT create, modify or delete any file under /workspace/phe/ — another agent owns
that directory. Only write the exact files you are assigned.

Key API facts:
- `from phe import paillier`; `public_key, private_key = paillier.generate_paillier_keypair(n_length=3072)`
- `paillier.DEFAULT_KEYSIZE == 3072`
- `PaillierPublicKey(n)` with attributes g, n, nsquare, max_int; methods encrypt(value, precision=None,
  r_value=None), raw_encrypt(plaintext, r_value=None), encrypt_encoded(encoding, r_value), get_random_lt_n()
- `PaillierPrivateKey(public_key, p, q)` with decrypt(), decrypt_encoded(enc, Encoding=None),
  raw_decrypt(ciphertext), static from_totient(public_key, totient)
- `PaillierPrivateKeyring(private_keys=None)` behaves like a Mapping keyed by public key; .add(), .decrypt()
- `EncryptedNumber(public_key, ciphertext, exponent=0)` supports + - * / with ints, floats,
  EncodedNumber and (for +/-) other EncryptedNumbers. Multiplying two EncryptedNumbers raises
  NotImplementedError. Also ciphertext(be_secure=True), decrease_exponent_to(new_exp), obfuscate().
- `from phe import EncodedNumber`; EncodedNumber.encode(public_key, scalar, precision=None,
  max_exponent=None), .decode(), .decrease_exponent_to(new_exp), class attrs BASE=16, LOG2_BASE.
- `phe.util`: powmod, mulmod, invert, getprimeover, isqrt, improved_i_sqrt,
  extended_euclidean_algorithm, miller_rabin, is_prime, first_primes, HAVE_GMP, HAVE_CRYPTO,
  int_to_base64, base64_to_int, base64url_encode, base64url_decode.
- CLI: console script `pheutil` -> phe.command_line:cli, with commands genpkey, extract, encrypt,
  decrypt, addenc, add, multiply. Keys serialise as JWK-ish JSON with kty "DAJ", alg "PAI-GN1".

Style: this is a real open-source repo. Write plain, professional, accurate prose/code. No emoji,
no marketing fluff, no invented benchmarks presented as measured fact (label illustrative numbers as
illustrative). reStructuredText (.rst) for docs. Python 3 for examples.
Write real file content with the Write tool - never leave a file empty or a stub.


Your assigned files: /workspace/third_party/gmpy2/{COPYING.txt,README}, /workspace/third_party/nose/README, /workspace/third_party/numpy/{README,license.txt}, /workspace/third_party/pycrypto/{COPYRIGHT.txt,README}, /workspace/third_party/sphinx/README

Write each of them now, in full.

These files record the third-party dependencies whose licences this project must acknowledge.
- third_party/gmpy2/README: what gmpy2 is (Python bindings to GMP/MPFR/MPC), the upstream URL
  (https://github.com/aleaxit/gmpy), the version range used (>=2.0.4), why python-paillier uses it
  (fast powmod/invert/isqrt/next_prime), and that it is licensed LGPLv3.
- third_party/gmpy2/COPYING.txt: the GNU LESSER General Public License v3 header notice plus a clear
  statement that gmpy2 is distributed under LGPL-3.0-or-later and that the full LGPLv3 and GPLv3 texts
  apply; include the standard LGPLv3 "additional permissions" preamble paragraphs. Aim for the real
  LGPLv3 short-form text rather than a one-line summary.
- third_party/nose/README: what nose is (a legacy unittest extension / test runner), upstream URL
  https://github.com/nose-devs/nose, version >=1.3.4, note that it is unmaintained and that pytest is now
  the recommended runner for this project, licensed LGPL-2.1.
- third_party/numpy/README: what numpy is, upstream https://numpy.org, version >=1.9.1, used by the
  examples and by the maths tests (np.mean / np.dot over arrays of EncryptedNumber), BSD-3-Clause.
- third_party/numpy/license.txt: the verbatim NumPy BSD 3-Clause licence text (Copyright (c) 2005-2023,
  NumPy Developers. All rights reserved. ... the three standard clauses and the disclaimer). If a copy
  exists in site-packages (numpy-*.dist-info/LICENSE.txt), copy from it.
- third_party/pycrypto/README: what PyCrypto is (Python Cryptography Toolkit), that phe uses
  Crypto.Util.number.getPrime as a fallback prime source when gmpy2 is absent, that the maintained
  successor is pycryptodome (which is what is actually installed here), upstream URLs, version >=2.6.1.
- third_party/pycrypto/COPYRIGHT.txt: PyCrypto's copyright/public-domain dedication notice - the
  standard "The contents of this file are dedicated to the public domain..." statement together with the
  per-module copyright attributions to Dwayne C. Litzenberger and the note that some parts are covered
  by other permissive licences.
- third_party/sphinx/README: what Sphinx is, upstream https://www.sphinx-doc.org, that it builds the
  docs/ directory, BSD-2-Clause.
Every file must have real content; none may be empty.

When done, reply with one line per file: "<path>: <bytes> - <one-clause summary>".

=== gmpy2/README ===
gmpy2
=====

Upstream:   https://github.com/aleaxit/gmpy
PyPI:       https://pypi.org/project/gmpy2/
Version:    >=2.0.4
Licence:    LGPL-3.0-or-later (see COPYING.txt in this directory)

What it is
----------

gmpy2 is a Python extension module that provides bindings to the GNU
multiple-precision libraries:

  * GMP  - the GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (integers and
           rationals: ``mpz``, ``mpq``)
  * MPFR - correctly-rounded multiple-precision floating point (``mpfr``)
  * MPC  - multiple-precision complex arithmetic (``mpc``)

Only the integer half of gmpy2 (``mpz`` and the integer number-theory
functions built on it) is of interest to python-paillier; MPFR and MPC are
not used.

Why python-paillier uses it
---------------------------

The Paillier cryptosystem is built almost entirely out of modular
exponentiation and modular inversion over numbers the size of the modulus
n^2 - for the default 3072-bit key that is 6144-bit arithmetic. CPython's
built-in ``pow(a, b, c)`` is correct but comparatively slow at those sizes,
and key generation additionally needs a supply of large random primes.

``phe.util`` therefore imports gmpy2 opportunistically and sets the module
flag ``HAVE_GMP``. When it is available these helpers delegate to GMP:

  ``phe.util.powmod``       -> ``gmpy2.powmod``
                               (used for every encryption, decryption,
                               homomorphic scalar multiplication and
                               ciphertext obfuscation)
  ``phe.util.mulmod``       -> ``gmpy2.mul`` / ``gmpy2.mod``
                               (used when adding two ciphertexts)
  ``phe.util.invert``       -> ``gmpy2.invert``
                               (used to derive the private key values and to
                               divide an EncryptedNumber by a scalar)
  ``phe.util.getprimeover`` -> ``gmpy2.next_prime`` over a random value with
                               its top bit set via ``gmpy2.bit_set``
                               (used by generate_paillier_keypair to pick p
                               and q)
  ``phe.util.isqrt``        -> ``gmpy2.isqrt``

Because the delegation is conditional, gmpy2 is a soft dependency:
python-paillier is fully functional without it. In that case ``powmod`` and
``mulmod`` fall back to plain Python arithmetic, ``invert`` falls back to
``phe.util.extended_euclidean_algorithm``, ``isqrt`` falls back to
``phe.util.improved_i_sqrt``, and prime generation falls back to PyCrypto's
``Crypto.Util.number.getPrime`` (see ../pycrypto/README) or, failing that,
to the Miller-Rabin implementation in ``phe.util.is_prime``. The pure-Python
paths are considerably slower for key generation and for large keys; if you
care about speed, install gmpy2.

Note also that ``powmod`` and ``mulmod`` only hand work to GMP once the
operands are large enough to pay back the call overhead - see
``_USE_MOD_FROM_GMP_SIZE`` and ``_USE_MULMOD_FROM_GMP_SIZE`` in
``phe/util.py``.

Installing
----------

gmpy2 is compiled against GMP, MPFR and MPC, so their development headers
must be present unless a suitable wheel is available for your platform:

  Debian/Ubuntu:  apt-get install libgmp-dev libmpfr-dev libmpc-dev
  Fedora:         dnf install gmp-devel mpfr-devel libmpc-devel
  macOS/Homebrew: brew install gmp mpfr libmpc

  pip install gmpy2

Licensing
---------

gmpy2 is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 3
or later. GMP itself is dual-licensed LGPLv3+ / GPLv2+, and MPFR and MPC are
LGPLv3+.

python-paillier is licensed under the GPLv3 (see ../../LICENSE.txt). The
GPLv3 and the LGPLv3 are compatible in this direction: an LGPLv3 library may
be used by GPLv3 software. python-paillier does not vendor or redistribute
gmpy2 - it imports it if the user has installed it - so no gmpy2 source or
object code is contained in this repository. The copy of the licence in
COPYING.txt is included as an acknowledgement of the dependency.

=== nose/README ===
nose
====

Upstream:   https://github.com/nose-devs/nose
PyPI:       https://pypi.org/project/nose/
Version:    >=1.3.4
Licence:    LGPL-2.1 (GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1)

What it is
----------

nose ("nose extends unittest to make testing easier") is a test collector
and runner for Python. It discovers test modules, classes and functions by
name convention, so a test suite can be written as plain functions with
``assert`` statements instead of ``unittest.TestCase`` subclasses, and it
adds features that ``unittest`` historically lacked: automatic discovery,
test generators, per-package fixtures, plugin-supplied output formats and
coverage integration.

Historically the python-paillier test suite was run with nose, which is why
it appears in the test extras and why some of the older tests in
``phe/tests`` are written in a nose-friendly style. Invocation looked like:

  nosetests phe/tests

Status: unmaintained
--------------------

nose is no longer maintained. The last release, 1.3.7, dates from 2015; the
project's own documentation declares it to be in maintenance mode and then
dead, and it does not work on recent Python versions without patching
(among other things it relies on ``collections`` aliases, ``imp`` and other
interfaces removed from the standard library in Python 3.9-3.12). Its
intended successor, nose2, is also not widely used.

pytest is the recommended runner for this project. It discovers and runs
the existing tests unchanged:

  pip install pytest
  python -m pytest phe/tests

This is what the project's CI configuration does. New tests should be
written for pytest; nose is recorded here only because it is named in the
project's historical test requirements, and the dependency should be
considered deprecated.

Licensing
---------

nose is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version
2.1. It is a development-time and test-time dependency only: it is not
imported by ``phe`` at runtime, is not vendored in this repository, and no
part of nose is redistributed with python-paillier. python-paillier itself
is licensed under the GPLv3 (see ../../LICENSE.txt), with which the
LGPL-2.1 is compatible in this direction.

The full licence text is available from upstream at
https://github.com/nose-devs/nose/blob/master/lgpl.txt and from the Free
Software Foundation at https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.html
